paras: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

The induction is a way to help you to pull your attention together so that you can hear material that might not reach you when you are soober. It is NOT something where you have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. If you are sober and having trouble focussing, too distracted, analytical, or are putting up a lot of resistance to working, an actual induction may help. However, if you are already pretty trancey from meditating beforehand, from loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, working through grief, hearing music, praying, being tired, or for any other reason, you may want to skip to orienting and making sure you are contained instead of adding depth.

paras: A shortcut back into hypnosis

Once you've learned a useful induction and also the full return below, you can make up your own shortcut for getting back under hypnosis. My dad used to do a mudra (hand sign) by bringing two fingers together in an "okay" sign, and it would help him relax. So keep the cue you use for calming yourself while alert separate from the one for going into inward hypnosis!

paras: Choose a Unique Word, Phrase or Movement You may want to add a gesture, but it's not necessary. You are giving that word, phrase or gesture a meaning that you choose.

When you are in a place and time where you have set aside time and it is appropriate and you want to deliberately start hypnosis with your short cut, then you can return to this familiar way of listening, from where you can change the direction of your experience or end the hypnosis.
